deities: Jalpa Devi / Awah Devi (worshipped by locals as Kul Devi)

history.summary: Hilltop shrine on the Hamirpur-Mandi border, said to be over 250-275 years old (verify). Legend says the pindi (stone form) of the goddess was unearthed by farmers ploughing a field; when people of Mandi tried to carry it to their side, they turned blind until they returned it, so the idol was installed where it now stands on the highest point of Hamirpur. An alternate telling links the name to the Pandavas' exclamation 'Wah Devi' here. Built by local people; the complex also houses a Guga Pir idol. CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column holds the town name 'Hamirpur'; the temple is in Himachal Pradesh.

name: Awah Devi Temple
town_description: Awah Devi is a hilltop settlement in Bhoranj tehsil, about 24 km from Hamirpur town on the Sarkaghat road at the Hamirpur-Mandi border. The temple crowns the hill said to be the highest point of Hamirpur, with wide views over the surrounding valleys.
